parsed.explanation: The combined regime documents no trans-specific criminal offence, no facility-access statute, and no documented pattern of police or border targeting of trans visitors; the deliberately-not-counted section records these as unknowns, not as safety. Offsetting this, legal protections are thin and stalled: no explicit anti-discrimination law, no hate-crime recognition, marriage and partner recognition closed, and a strongly conservative public climate (12% approval of same-sex marriage; organised religious opposition). A visitor in a relationship read as same-sex has no recognition and no remedy, and recourse for service refusal or hostility is essentially absent. Resident-facing gaps (surgery-based recognition, no LGR reform) are climate signals only. The indigenous third-gender acceptance is one localized data point. Result: no state-imposed exposure, but thin recourse in a disapproving society.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border handling of mismatched gender markers; dossier explicitly records no located screening, secondary inspection or detention on that basis — an open question, not a documented harm.
entry_documents.protection: Gender change is legally permitted domestically (surgery required), suggesting no blanket bar on gender-diverse status; same-sex activity is legal.
entry_documents.interaction: Unknown border practice could interact with conservative social attitudes if documents are examined; no evidence either way.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented detention, arrest or custody practice targeting trans visitors; no trans-specific criminal provision exists.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Legal same-sex activity and absence of trans-criminalisation remove the usual custody pathway; courts engage (if slowly) with rights claims.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Conservative framing of gender nonconformity as immoral could colour any police encounter, but no record supports this for visitors.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No statute governing bathroom, changing-room or single-sex facility access was located; practical rules are undocumented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Private venues operating in a conservative climate may set their own rules without statutory constraint or remedy.

care_services.exposure: No documented emergency-care denial to trans visitors; conversion therapy is not banned (mainly resident-facing).
care_services.protection: Gender-affirming change of status is legally recognized domestically, implying some clinical infrastructure; same-sex legality reduces morality-law leverage in care settings.
care_services.interaction: Care access for a traveller is undocumented; blood-donation deferral affects gay men, tangentially reaching some trans visitors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Constitutional Article 39 used to refuse gay-organisation registration; dominant religious institution opposes recognition; a legislator's dehumanising rhetoric; no hate-crime charge exists for identity-motivated violence.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Legislature withdrew constitutional same-sex marriage ban before referendum amid protests; government signalled compliance with regional human-rights court; First Lady supported equality litigation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing is directed at relationships more than gender expression; a visitor read as being in a same-sex relationship inherits it with no recognition or remedy.

minors_guardians.exposure: No documented child-protection or custody rule triggered by a trans parent or accompanying minor; conservative climate could draw scrutiny in family settings.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented restriction on a trans adult travelling with a minor.
minors_guardians.interaction: Unresolved: how officials or services would treat a travelling family whose composition reads as gender-diverse.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No recorded trans killings, no documented police targeting pattern, no organised targeting; no hate-crime recognition means identity-motivated violence would not be charged or recorded as such.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Same-sex conduct legal; no trans-specific violence record in the sources.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of a hate-crime category means any incident would be handled as ordinary crime, removing a signal rather than creating one.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Anti-discrimination amendment blocked in 2024; 2015 bill stalled; no employment/housing protections; UPR states report stalled reforms — recourse for service refusal or hostility is effectively absent.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts function and engaged with rights claims; regional human-rights court compliance was signalled; civil society and amicus advocacy exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Working institutions do not enforce a protection that does not exist; conservative social climate plus thin legal remedy is the operative combination.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower: Vellandra has a routine, enforced border register excluding transgender visitors with no remedy — a universal-exposure mechanism. This dossier documents no border restriction, no registration, and no exclusion at all; its worst feature is absent recognition and thin recourse, not active exclusion.

Similar-to-slightly-higher: Qorinda shows private hostility with functioning courts that deliver real remedies (injunction, damages, fine). Here institutions function but there is no anti-discrimination law to invoke, so recourse is thinner — yet there is also no documented extortion or hostile-neighbour pattern against visitors.

Lower: Meridia documents trained, respectful border inspection, accepted markers, and a working tribunal with compensation. This dossier has none of that documented machinery — no evidence of respectful screening or remedy — so it cannot reach that tier despite equally lacking criminalisation.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a conservative, religiously-influenced society with no trans-specific criminal law, no documented police or border targeting, and no facility statute — meaning no tier-1 or tier-2 exposure is documented for a visitor. What dominates instead is tier-3: a disapproving public climate, closed marriage/partner recognition with no route for a relationship read as same-sex, and effectively no legal recourse (blocked anti-discrimination amendment, no hate-crime charge, stalled reforms) if the traveller experiences service refusal or hostility. Resident-facing gaps are climate signals only. Open questions (border document handling, facility practice, care for visitors) are unknowns, not exposures, but they prevent a higher score because absence of documentation here does not establish safety. Adult solo travellers and travelling families face the same undocumented-entry, thin-recourse profile; nothing in the dossier differentiates minors.
